articleTitle: A computer study of the calibration of the skeletal biconical antenna and the resonant dipole antenna
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiated Emission Test Facilities
abstract: The plane-wave antenna factors of the resonant dipole antenna and the skeletal biconical antenna are derived from a computer simulation approach in order to obtain accurate values. The method for calibration of the skeletal biconical antenna also shows how the effects of a balun may be incorporated into a theoretical antenna factor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A transmission-line modelling (TLM) study of screened room behaviour
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiated Emission Test Facilities
abstract: The importance of numerical modelling using TLM when applied to screened rooms is described. Examples are given to show determination of resonances, the effects of absorbing material and field profiles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new ferrite grid absorber for screened rooms
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiated Emission Test Facilities
abstract: Describes a new ferrite grid absorber panel which shows substantially improved reflectivity over conventional ferrite tiles. This allows screened 3 m (or larger) test ranges to be constructed for radiated emission testing. Existing rooms can readily be converted to improve their usability for both emissions and susceptibility measurements. The availability, using this material, of screened chambers of moderate size and cost will enable test facilities to make more accurate, repeatable and reliable measurements, that are unaffected by environmental or ambient factors, for the purpose of demonstrating compliance with the EMC Directive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a climatically controlled reverberating chamber for the measurement of total radiated power
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiated Emission Test Facilities
abstract: Presents the development of a low cost climatically controlled reverberating chamber (CCRC) measurement facility by modifying a suitable environmental chamber in order to produce time-averaged isotropic field conditions over the frequency band 12 to 60 GHz and demonstrates its use over a range of temperatures from -20 degrees C to +40 degrees C.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of a high voltage laboratory as an open area test site
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiated Emission Test Facilities
abstract: Explores the possibility of using a large existing laboratory to house an open area test site (OATS). The results of preliminary tests on an OATS housed inside a large semi-shielded enclosure appear promising. However testing will have to be carried out on a full size ground plane of at least 6 m*5.2 m, for horizontal as well as vertical polarization and the frequency range will need to be extended down to 30 MHz. The major source of error appears to be the presence of a conductive ceiling. However the large size of the laboratory, coupled with its imperfect 'shielded' construction has resulted in a desirable lack of resonances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A compact range using and array antenna
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radiated Emission Test Facilities
abstract: The use of an array of log-periodic dipole antennas for compact range illumination has been under investigation at Bradford University. A seven-element array has been built to demonstrate the principle and latest developments of the work are reported. The system has been demonstrated to have an excellent performance, giving a 'quiet zone' satisfying EMC criteria that is as wide as the aperture itself, compared with typically one-third of the width for a reflector antenna.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
